items.title: The Ocular Examination / Ocular Emergencies (Triage Overview)
items.summary: OP.S03's raw TOC title is the concatenated 'OcularEmergencies', but merged_duplicate_headings records a co-located real heading, 'The Ocular Examination', on the same OP5-OP6 page span. Both headings are clinically substantive (unlike the OB.S01/NS.S01 acronym-glossary precedent, where one of two co-located headings was non-clinical and safely discarded), so both are represented as separate study units from the same single source node, following the OB.S07 compound-title-split precedent. The true page boundary between the two headings could not be determined from the TOC alone.
items.recommended_action: Reviewer should confirm against the source PDF (pdf pages 1045-1046, TN OP5-OP6) whether 'The Ocular Examination' and 'Ocular Emergencies' are in fact two adjacent headings (in which case the split is correct and page ranges could be tightened) or whether the OCR extraction genuinely merged/mislabeled a single section (in which case one of SU-OP-11/SU-OP-12 may need to be retired or retitled).

items.title: Malignancies / Ocular Manifestations of Systemic Disease (OP.S15 dual-theme section)
items.summary: OP.S15's raw TOC title is 'Malignancies', but merged_duplicate_headings records a co-located real heading, 'Ocular Manifestations of Systemic Disease', on the same OP33-OP36 span. The section's 13 topic children in fact span two distinct clinical themes (ocular malignancy: lid carcinoma/uveal melanoma/metastases; and systemic-disease ocular manifestations: HIV, diabetes, hypertension, MS, Graves', connective tissue disease, GCA, sarcoidosis). Represented as one malignancy-themed unit (SU-OP-42) and seven systemic-disease-themed units (SU-OP-43 to SU-OP-49) grouped by clinical theme rather than raw section title, since no page-level boundary between the two themes is recoverable from the TOC.
items.recommended_action: Reviewer should confirm the theme-based regrouping against the source PDF (pdf pages 1073-1076, TN OP33-OP36) and verify no topic was misassigned to the wrong theme (e.g., confirm HIV/AIDS at OP.S15.T04 is presented as a systemic-disease-ocular-manifestation topic rather than an ocular-malignancy-risk topic in the original text).

items.title: Uveitis / Common Medications ('The Uveal Tract' unresolved heading)
items.summary: RESOLVED (targeted follow-up, 2026-08-26). research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json's UNRESOLVED candidate 'The Uveal Tract' (raw_ocr_line 'The UvealTract (c). 2... ee OP20 ou') was independently resolved via raw OCR of the chapter's own TOC page (pdf 1041) and body pages 1060-1061. Finding: 'The Uveal Tract' is a real, body-confirmed heading at pdf 1060 (TN OP20) introducing genuine 'Uveitis' clinical content (etiology incl. HLA-B27 spondyloarthropathies, anatomic classification, complications, treatment) spanning pdf 1060-1061 -- immediately followed by LENS/Cataracts on the same page 1061, NOT by OP.S19 at OP44-45 as originally (incorrectly) sourced. The original 'Uveitis Common Medications' TOC line the pipeline built OP.S19 from is itself a two-column OCR merge of the stray 'Uveitis' index entry (pointing to OP20, same as 'The Uveal Tract') and the real 'Common Medications' heading at OP44 (which body-confirms as a pure ophthalmic-medications reference table with no uveitis content). Corrected: SU-OP-60 ('Uveitis') is now sourced from a synthetic UNCATALOGUED:TheUvealTract@pdf1060 id (per the chapter-A 'Monitoring' precedent, since no toc_inventory.json node exists for this dropped heading) with tn_page_range OP20-OP21 / pdf_page_range [1060,1061]; SU-OP-61 is retitled 'Common Medications (Ophthalmic Reference Table)' and its rationale corrected to remove the stray Uveitis attribution, remaining sourced from OP.S19 (OP44-45) unchanged. No reclassification or MCC-evidence change was made to either unit -- the content was already represented, only mis-sourced.
items.recommended_action: None -- resolved. No further action required; the chapter-A-precedent 'add a toc_inventory.json node for the dropped heading' remediation remains available for a future TOC-extraction pass but is not required for this chapter's own crosswalk to be valid, per the same precedent.

items.title: Multiple study units carry only WEAK MCC evidence (no dedicated ophthalmology-specific MCC objective)
items.summary: A full-registry search-mcc-objectives sweep for 'cataract', 'glaucoma', 'floaters', 'macular degeneration', 'diabetic retinopathy', 'orbital cellulitis', 'corneal', 'hyphema', 'leukocoria', 'ptosis', 'conjunctivitis', 'retinal detachment', 'temporal arteritis', 'chemical burn', 'amaurosis', 'photophobia', 'ocular', 'arteritis', 'vasculitis', 'eyelid', 'stye', 'blepharitis', 'dry eye', 'uveitis', 'iritis', 'keratitis', 'scleritis', 'nystagmus', 'pupil', 'papilledema', 'optic neuritis', and 'orbit' returned zero direct matches for most of these terms (only 'dry eye' incidentally matched objective 30 Eye redness, and 'eye trauma' matched objective 109). The MCC Objectives registry has no ophthalmology-subspecialty presentation list beyond Eye redness (30), Acute/Chronic visual disturbance or loss (115-1/115-2), Diplopia (23), and Strabismus/amblyopia (102); most disease-specific ophthalmic entities (cataract, glaucoma, retinal vascular occlusion, orbital cellulitis, corneal ulcer, uveitis, etc.) are therefore mapped as COMPONENT/CROSS_DISCIPLINE against these five broader presentation-level objectives (or, for diabetic retinopathy/hypertensive retinopathy, against the nearest systemic-disease objective: 130 Hyperglycemia, 9-1 Hypertension) rather than against a dedicated objective, consistent with project accuracy rules (WEAK/UNCERTAIN rather than fabricated DIRECT evidence).
items.recommended_action: None required at this stage -- consistent with project accuracy rules (no invented MCC IDs; WEAK used where evidence is indirect). Coordinator may wish to note, in a future cross-chapter registry-gap audit, that the MCC Objectives Online registry itself appears to lack dedicated objectives for several high-prevalence ophthalmic diagnoses (cataract, glaucoma, retinal detachment/vascular occlusion) despite their presentation-level objectives (Eye redness, Vision loss) existing.
